q: The Shore Temple of the Mahabalipuram was:
options: built by the Chalukyas
built by the Pallava king Narasimhavarman I
built by the Rajaraja Chola
built by the Vijayanagara
explanation: The Shore Temple of the Mahabalipuram, a World Heritage site, was built by the Pallava king Narasimhavarman I in the early eighth century.

q: The 'Kailasanatha' of the Kanchipuram:
options: Is a Vijayanagara temple
Is a rock-cut replica of the Ellora Kailasa in the stone
Is a Chola temple
Is a Buddhist monastery
explanation: The Kailasanatha temple of the Kanchipuram was built by the Pallava king Narasimhavarman I as a stone imitation of the rock-cut Kailasa of the Ellora.

q: The Mamallapuram was:
options: the port of the Vijayanagara
the capital of the Gangas
the port of the Pallavas and the Rathas were the experimental ones
the port of the Cholas
explanation: The Mamallapuram was the port of the Pallava kings and the five monolithic Rathas and the Mandapas were the experiments of the sculptural art of the period.

q: The Shore Temple of the Mamallapuram is:
options: a Chola temple
a Vijayanagara temple
a Buddhist monastery
the oldest of the Dravidian temples in the stone
explanation: The Shore Temple, built by the Narasimhavarman I, is the earliest of the Dravidian temples in the stone and it is a World Heritage site.

q: The 'Dashavatara' of the Mahabalipuram:
options: Is the relief of the ten avatars of Vishnu
It is a panel of the ten kings
It is the ten Rathas
It is a Mahabharata scene
explanation: The Dashavatara Cave of the Mahabalipuram has the relief of the ten avatars of Vishnu, and the Krishnanattam of Kerala also has the Dashavatara tradition.

q: The 'Ganesha Ratha' of the Mahabalipuram:
options: Is the monolithic ratha with the carved panels of the Shiva and the Vishnu and the Durga
It is a cave temple
It is a Chola temple
It is a fort
explanation: The Ganesha Ratha, a monolithic ratha, is carved with the life-size panels of the Shiva, the Vishnu and the Durga.

q: The Otteri of the Mahabalipuram is:
options: It is a large temple
It is a chariot
It is a monastery
Is a small rock-cut temple of the Mahabalipuram with the Shiva and the Vishnu
explanation: The Otteri is a small rock-cut temple of the Mahabalipuram with the life-size panels of the Shiva and the Vishnu, and it is a fine example of the Pallava art.

q: The Somapura of the Banteay Srei is:
options: It is a temple of the Kerala
Is the great temple of the Banteay Srei in the Cambodia and the name means the Temple of the City
It is a temple of the Odisha
It is a temple of the Tamil Nadu
explanation: The Somapura, the great temple of the Banteay Srei in the Cambodia, was built by the Suryavarman II and the name means the 'Temple of the City'.

q: The 'Angkor Wat' was built by:
options: The Pagan king
The Sri Lankan king
Surya Varman II of the Khmer Empire
The Champa king
explanation: The Angkor Wat, the largest religious monument of the world, was built by the Khmer king Surya Varman II in the early twelfth century.

q: The 'Borobudur' of Indonesia:
options: It is a Hindu temple
It is a mosque
It is a Jain temple
Is the largest Buddhist monument of the world and was built by the Sailendra dynasty
explanation: The Borobudur, the largest Buddhist monument of the world, was built by the Sailendra dynasty of the Java and it is a World Heritage site.

q: The Wat Phra of the Bangkok is:
options: It is in the Borobudur
It is in the Peking
Is the Temple of the Emerald Buddha in the Bangkok and a World Heritage site
It is in the Angkor
explanation: The Wat Phra, the royal temple of the Emerald Buddha in the Bangkok, was inscribed as a World Heritage site in 1992.

q: The 'Potala' of Tibet:
options: It is a fort in the Nepal
Is the winter palace of the Dalai Lama at the Lhasa and a World Heritage site
It is a mosque
It is a Hindu temple
explanation: The Potala Palace, the winter palace of the Dalai Lama at the Lhasa, was inscribed as a World Heritage site in 1994.

q: The 'Diwan-i-Khas' of the Fatehpur Sikri:
options: Has the famous iron pillar with the inscription of the Ashoka
It has the Taj Mahal's cenotaph
It has the marble throne
It has the Charminar
explanation: The Diwan-i-Khas of the Fatehpur Sikri has the iron pillar with the inscription of the Ashoka that was brought from Delhi.

q: The tomb of the Itimad-ud-Daulah is:
options: in the Delhi
the first of the Mughal tombs at the Agra and the first to use the white marble
the tomb of the Akbar
the tomb of the Jahangir
explanation: The tomb of the Itimad-ud-Daulah, the first of the Mughal tombs at the Agra and the first to use the white marble, is the precursor of the Taj Mahal.

q: Jama Masjid is:
options: It is a Jain temple
It is a Chola temple
It is in the Delhi
Is the largest of the Mughal mosque complexes with the Jai Mandir of the Akbar
explanation: The Jama Masjid of the Fatehpur Sikri, with the Jai Mandir adjoining it, is the largest of the individual Mughal mosque complexes and it shows the congregational use of the space.

q: Which of the following statements about the Agra Fort is correct?
options: It is a fort of the Rajputs
It is a fort of the Portuguese
Is the Red Fort of the Agra built by the Akbar and it has the Diwan-i-Khas of the Shah Jahan
It is the Red Fort of the Delhi
explanation: The Agra Fort, the Red Fort of the Agra, was built by the Akbar and it was completed by the Shah Jahan, who added the Diwan-i-Khas with the Musamman Burj.

q: The Itimad-ud-Daulah mausoleum of the Agra is:
options: built entirely of the white marble and it is the precursor of the Taj Mahal
built of the red sandstone
in the Delhi
the tomb of the Akbar
explanation: The tomb of the Itimad-ud-Daulah, built entirely of the white marble with the pietra dura, is the precursor of the Taj Mahal in the techniques and the aesthetics.

q: The golden age of the Mughal art is the period of:
options: There is no golden age
The Shah Jahan period is considered the golden age of the Mughal art
The Akbar period is the golden age
The Jahangir period is the golden age
explanation: The Shah Jahan period is considered the golden age of the Mughal art with the refined and the formal aesthetic and the masterpieces of the Taj Mahal and the Red Fort.

q: The Bichitr was a painter of the:
options: The Bichitr was a painter of the Jahangir's court and his portrait of the Jahangir is at the Bodleian
He was a painter of the Akbar's court
He was the son of the Man Singh
He was a painter of the Deccan
explanation: The Bichitr, the leading painter of the Jahangir's court, painted the famous portrait of the Jahangir that is now in the Bodleian Library at Oxford.

q: The Padshahnama, the Book of Kings is:
options: the chronicle of the Jahangir
a Jain text
the illustrated chronicle of the Shah Jahan's reign
the chronicle of the Akbar
explanation: The Padshahnama, the Book of Kings, is the illustrated chronicle of the Shah Jahan's reign and it was written by the Abdul Hamid Lahori with the 116 miniatures by the Bichitr and the other painters.

q: The 'Razmnama' of the Akbar:
options: It is the Persian translation of the Ramayana
It is a translation of the Atharvaveda
It is the biography of the Akbar
Is the Persian translation of the Mahabharata and it was done by the Naqd Ali Khan and the Bada Khair Khan
explanation: The Razmnama, the Book of Wars, was the Persian translation of the Mahabharata that was commissioned by the Akbar and it was completed by the Naqd Ali Khan and the Bada Khair Khan.

q: The 'Akbar Nama' of the Abul Fazl:
options: It is a book of the music
It is the Persian translation of the Mahabharata
Is the chronicle of the Akbar's reign and it has the Ain-i-Akbari
It is the biography of the Jahangir
explanation: The Akbar Nama, the chronicle of the Akbar's reign by the Abul Fazl, has the third volume, the Ain-i-Akbari, which describes the administration and the society.

q: The 'Hamzanama' of the Akbar:
options: Is the largest of the Mughal manuscripts with the illustrations of the Amir Hamza's adventures
It is the biography of the Akbar
It is a chronicle of the Shah Jahan
It is a Jain text
explanation: The Hamzanama, with about 140 illustrations, is the largest of the Mughal manuscripts and it narrates the adventures of the Amir Hamza.

q: The 'Tutinama' of the Akbar:
options: It is a Jain text
Is the illustrated manuscript of the tales of the parrot that was translated into the Persian
It is the chronicle of the Akbar
It is the poem of the Amir Hamza
explanation: The Tutinama, the Book of the Parrot, was the manuscript of the tales that the Akbar had translated into the Persian from the Hindi.

q: The paintings patronised by the Jahangir are:
options: He preferred the narrative paintings
He did not patronise the painting
He preferred only the religious paintings
The Jahangir preferred the allegorical and the single figure portraits and the calligraphic work
explanation: The Jahangir preferred the single figure portraits, the allegorical compositions and the calligraphic works, in contrast to the narrative approach of the Akbar.

q: The 'Golden Apple' of the Jahangir:
options: It is a portrait of the Akbar
Is an allegorical composition of the Jahangir holding the globe with the butterflies and the cherubs
It is a portrait of the Jahangir
It is a hunting scene
explanation: The Golden Apple, of the allegorical type, shows the Jahangir holding the globe with the cherubs and the butterflies and it is in the collection of the Los Angeles County Museum.

q: The Shah Jahan of the Mughal painting preferred:
options: He did not patronise the painting
He preferred only the hunting scenes
The Shah Jahan preferred the formal and the portraiture and the court scenes
He preferred the allegorical works
explanation: The Shah Jahan preferred the formal compositions, the portraiture and the court scenes, and the Mughal album of the period is the model of the refined aesthetic.

q: The Aurangzeb period of the Mughal painting is:
options: It was the golden age of the painting
He was the patron of the European painters
The painting flourished in his reign
The Aurangzeb period is noted for the decline of the painting and the increase of the religious and the calligraphic work
explanation: The Aurangzeb period is marked by the decline of the painting and the growth of the religious and the calligraphic work, as the emperor withdrew his patronage from the painters.

q: The 'Pahari' schools of the painting:
options: Include the Kangra, the Guler, the Bashahr and the Mandi
Include only the Jaipur and the Mewar
They are of the Deccan
They are of Bengal
explanation: The Pahari schools, the hill painting, include the Kangra, the Guler, the Bashahr and the Mandi and they flourished in the 17th and the 18th centuries.

q: The 'Bundi' school of the painting:
options: Is the Rajasthani school known for the bold colours and the flat treatment
It is the Mughal school
It is the Company style
It is the Bengal school
explanation: The Bundi school, the Hindoli and the Kotah, are known for the bold colours, the flat treatment and the intimate and the devotional themes.

q: The 'Deccani' schools of the painting:
options: They are the Rajasthani schools
They are the Pahari schools
They are the Bengali schools
Include the Bijapur, the Golconda and the Ahmadnagar and the style is Deccani with the Persian and the Indian elements
explanation: The Deccani schools of the Bijapur, the Golconda and the Ahmadnagar have a distinct style with the Persian and the Indian elements and the literary and the devotional themes.

q: The Bengal school was:
options: the school of the photo printing
founded by the Abanindranath Tagore and it revived the Indian tradition
founded by the M.F. Husain
a revival of the European realism
explanation: The Bengal school, founded by the Abanindranath Tagore, revived the Indian and the Japanese traditions as a reaction to the academic realism of the Company painting.

q: The 'Jamini Roy' was:
options: A painter of the Madras Movement
A sculptor
A painter of the Bengal school who used the Kalighat and the Pat style
A painter of the Bombay Progressive Artists' Group
explanation: The Jamini Roy, the most famous of the Bengal school painters, adapted the Kalighat and the Pat styles with the bold outlines and the flat colours.

q: The Abanindranath Tagore was:
options: He painted theBharat Mata and the older Indian themes
He painted the modern cityscapes
He was the founder of the Madras Movement
He was a disciple of the Amrita Sher-Gil
explanation: The Abanindranath Tagore painted the Bharat Mata, the older Indian themes and the Mughal style, and he founded the Kala Bhavana at the Santiniketan.

q: Raja Ravi Varma is best remembered for:
options: He founded the Madras Movement
He was a member of the Progressive Artists' Group
He reformed the Indian painting with the academic realism and the oil technique
He founded the Bengal school
explanation: The Raja Ravi Varma reformed the Indian painting with the academic realism and the oil technique and the oleographs of the mythological themes reached the villages.

q: The Madras Art Movement was:
options: led by the M.F. Husain
the movement of the Bengal school
a European movement
led by the D.P. Roy Chowdhury and the K.C.S. Paniker
explanation: The Madras Art Movement, led by the D.P. Roy Chowdhury, the K.C.S. Paniker and the S. Dhanapal, was the south Indian counterpart of the progressive art movements.

q: Sadanand Bakre was:
options: a painter of the Madras Movement
a painter of the Bombay Progressive Artists' Group who died young
a painter of the Bengal school
the founder of the Kalakshetra
explanation: The Sadanand Bakre, a member of the Progressive Artists' Group, died young at 27 and his work is in the National Gallery of Modern Art.

q: The 'Ram Kumar' was:
options: A folk painter
A painter of the post-independence India who painted the landscapes and the still lifes
A painter of the Bengal school
A sculptor
explanation: The Ram Kumar was one of the leading painters of the post-independence India and his landscapes and the still lifes are marked by the depth of the colour.

q: The 'Tyeb Mehta' was:
options: A painter who used the falling figures and the bulls and the simple forms
A painter of the Bengal school
A sculptor of the Chola bronzes
A folk painter of the Rajasthan
explanation: The Tyeb Mehta, one of the leading painters of the modern India, is known for the bulls, the falling figures and the simple and the flat forms.

q: The 'Akbar Padamsee' was:
options: A painter of the Bengal school
A sculptor
A folk painter
A painter of the Bombay Progressive Artists' Group and a founder of the Jehangir Art Gallery
explanation: The Akbar Padamsee, a member of the Progressive Artists' Group, was a founder of the Jehangir Art Gallery in Mumbai and the chairman of the National Gallery of Modern Art.

q: The 'Sankho Chaudhuri' was:
options: A sculptor
A film director
A painter of the modern India known for the human figures and the horses
A painter of the Bengal school
explanation: The Sankho Chaudhuri is a painter of the modern India who is known for the human figures and the horses with the muted palette.

q: The K.G. Subramanyan is best known for:
options: He used the Indian folk idioms and the mythology in his work
He painted the European still lifes
He was the founder of the Madras Movement
He was the disciple of the Raja Ravi Varma
explanation: The K.G. Subramanyan drew on the Indian folk idioms, the mythology and the epics in his paintings and the murals, and he was also a scholar of the folk traditions.

q: The 'V.S. Gaitonde' was:
options: A painter of the folk art
A sculptor
A printmaker
A painter of the abstract landscapes who was called the Enfant Terrible of the Indian art
explanation: The V.S. Gaitonde, the abstract painter of the landscapes, was called the 'Enfant Terrible' of the Indian art and he was the first Indian to represent his work in the documenta of the Venice Biennale.

q: She studied in Paris and her self portraits are:
options: a folk painter
celebrated for the psychological depth
a member of the Bengal school
a sculptor
explanation: The Amrita Sher-Gil, who studied in Paris, is celebrated for the psychological depth of her self portraits and the Hungarian and the Indian influences in her work.

q: The S.H. Raza was:
options: a sculptor
a folk painter
a founder of the Progressive Artists' Group and a painter of the geometric abstracts
a painter of the Bengal school
explanation: The S.H. Raza, a founder of the Progressive Artists' Group, is known for the geometric abstracts in the later phase of his work.

q: The 'Krishen Khanna' was:
options: A painter of the Bengal school
A sculptor
A folk painter
A painter of the modern India known for the street scenes and the common people
explanation: The Krishen Khanna is known for the vivid street scenes and the portraits of the common people, and he was the first Indian painter whose works were auctioned for more than a million dollars.

q: Baroda Painting is:
options: the mural of the Ajanta
the folk painting of the Bihar
the classical painting of the Thanjavur and the Mysore with the gesso and the gold foil
the miniature of the Rajasthan
explanation: The Baroda painting, the classical painting of the Thanjavur and the Mysore, is marked by the gesso base and the gold foil and the relief work.

q: The Kalighat painting of the Calcutta is known for:
options: Is the bold brushwork on the flat paper that developed around the Kalighat temple of the Calcutta
It is the miniature of the Rajasthan
It is the mural of the Ellora
It is the classical of the Thanjavur
explanation: The Kalighat painting developed in the nineteenth century around the Kalighat temple of the Calcutta with the bold brushwork, the flat paper and the imported colours.

q: The Madhubani painting of the Bihar is known for:
options: It is the classical of the Thanjavur
Is the Mithila painting with the bold geometric patterns and the double line borders
It is the miniature of the Rajasthan
It is the mural of the Karnataka
explanation: The Madhubani painting of the Bihar, the Mithila school, is known for the bold geometric patterns, the double line borders and the natural dyes.

q: The Warli painting of the Maharashtra is known for:
options: It is the gold foil work
It is the classical of the Mysore
Uses the simple stick figures of the white pigment on the mud brown background
It is the miniature of the Rajputs
explanation: The Warli painting of the Maharashtra uses the simple stick figures of the white pigment on the mud brown background and it depicts the daily life and the deities.

q: The 'Pattachitra' of the Odisha:
options: It is the mural of the Karnataka
It is the miniature of the Rajputs
It is the classical of the Thanjavur
Is the cloth scroll painting used as the temple curtain of the Jagannath at Puri
explanation: The Pattachitra of the Odisha and the Bengal is the cloth scroll painting that was traditionally used as the temple curtain of the Jagannath at Puri.

q: The Panchi painting is:
options: It is the classical of the Mysore
Is the Odia folk scroll painting with the palm leaf and the natural dyes
It is the miniature of the Rajputs
It is the mural of the Karnataka
explanation: The Panchi, the Odia folk scroll painting, is painted on the palm leaf and the cloth with the natural dyes and it narrates the mythological stories.

q: The Patua painters are:
options: Are the scroll painters of the West Bengal and the Bihar
They are the classical painters of the Tamil Nadu
They are the muralists of the Karnataka
They are the sculptors of Bengal
explanation: The Patuas are the traditional scroll painters of the West Bengal and the Bihar, and the community of the Kalighat and the Suvarnabhumi are the prominent.

q: The Chamba rumal of the Himachal Pradesh is:
options: It is a painted scroll of the Odisha
It is a mural of the Rajasthan
It is a classical painting of the Tamil Nadu
Is a double sided embroidered covering of the Himachal Pradesh
explanation: The Chamba rumal is the double sided embroidered covering of the Chamba region of the Himachal Pradesh, worked in the do-rukha stitch with the multicoloured designs.

q: The Pashmina is the fine wool of the:
options: Is the fine wool of the Changthangi goats of the Ladakh and the Kashmir
It is a silk of the Assam
It is a cotton of the Gujarat
It is a wool of the Australian Merino
explanation: The Pashmina is the fine wool of the Changthangi goats of the Ladakh and the Kashmir and the shawls of the region are among the finest in the world.

q: The Cashmere fibre is:
options: It is a silk of the Assam
It is a cotton of the Gujarat
Is the fine fibre of the Changthangi goats of the Ladakh and the Kashmir
It is a wool of the Australian Merino
explanation: The Cashmere is the fine undercoat fibre of the Changthangi goats and the Pashmina shawls are the best known product of it.

q: The Kinnow fruit is:
options: It is a grape variety
Is a citrus fruit grown in the Punjab and the Rajasthan
It is a variety of the apple
It is a mango variety
explanation: The Kinnow, a hybrid of the lemon and the orange, is grown in the Punjab, the Rajasthan and the Haryana and it is a GI tagged product.

q: Toda embroidery of the Nilgiris is is known:
options: Is known for the black and the white geometric motifs
It is the gold zari work of the Varanasi
It is the tie and dye of the Gujarat
It is the block print of the Rajasthan
explanation: The Toda embroidery of the Nilgiri hills is known for the black and the white geometric motifs with the characteristic black squares and stripes.

q: The Kashmir Shawl is:
options: It is a silk of the Assam
It is a cotton of the Gujarat
It is a gold brocade of the Tamil Nadu
Is a GI tagged product of the Kashmir and it is a handwoven woollen shawl
explanation: The Kashmir shawl, the Kani shawl, is a GI tagged handwoven woollen product of the Kashmir and it was given the GI tag in 2006-07.

q: The Mirzapur carpet is:
options: a cotton rug of the Gujarat
a plastic mat
a GI tagged hand-knotted woollen carpet of the Uttar Pradesh
a silk carpet of the Kashmir
explanation: The Mirzapur carpet, a hand-knotted woollen carpet of the Uttar Pradesh, is a GI tagged product and it is a major export.

q: The Thanjavur painting of the Tamil Nadu is:
options: It is the tie and dye
The Thanjavur painting uses the gold foil on the teak panels with the gesso base
It is the miniature of the Rajasthan
It is the mural of the Karnataka
explanation: The Thanjavur painting of the Tamil Nadu, also called the Tanjore painting, uses the gold foil on the teak panels over a gesso base.

q: The Bandhani of the Gujarat and the Rajasthan is:
options: It is the painting of the Odisha
Is the tie and dye of the Gujarat and the Rajasthan
It is the embroidery of the Punjab
It is the block print of the Rajasthan
explanation: The Bandhani, the tie and dye with the tiny knots tied before the dyeing, is the traditional craft of the Gujarat and the Rajasthan.

q: The 'Zardozi' of Lucknow:
options: Is the metallic embroidery with the gold and the silver threads
It is the tie and dye
It is the block print
It is the ivory carving
explanation: The Zardozi, the metallic embroidery with the gold and the silver threads and the precious stones, reached its peak in the court of the Naw-awad.

q: The 'Khurja pottery' of the Uttar Pradesh:
options: It is the black pottery of the Khurja
It is the terracotta of the Odisha
It is the stoneware of the Assam
Is the glazed pottery and it is a GI tagged product
explanation: The Khurja pottery, the glazed pottery of the Khurja in the Uttar Pradesh, is a GI tagged product of the state.

q: The Banarasi silk of the Varanasi is:
options: It is a wool of the Ludhiana
It is a muslin of the Dhubai
Is a GI tagged brocade of the Varanasi with the zari
It is a cotton of the Coimbatore
explanation: The Banarasi silk, the zari brocade of the Varanasi, is a GI tagged product and the Kanjeevaram of the Tamil Nadu is the other famous one.

q: The 'Kanjeevaram' of the Tamil Nadu:
options: It is a cotton sari of the Coimbatore
It is a muslin of the Bengal
It is a shawl of the Kashmir
Is a GI tagged silk sari with the contrasting borders and the zari
explanation: The Kanjeevaram, with the bold colours, the contrasting borders and the zari, is a GI tagged silk sari of the Tamil Nadu.

q: The Khadi of the handspun yarn is:
options: It is a cotton of the Gujarat
Is the handwoven cloth of the handspun yarn and it is a GI tagged product
It is a silk of the Assam
It is a wool of the Kashmir
explanation: The Khadi, the handwoven cloth of the handspun yarn, is a GI tagged product and it was promoted by the Mahatma Gandhi as the symbol of the Swadeshi.

q: The Toda community of the Nilgiris is known:
options: a fishing community of the Konkan
a trading community of the Assam
for the pashmina shawls and the embroidery
a martial tribe of the Rajasthan
explanation: The Toda community of the Nilgiri hills is known for the pashmina shawls that they weave and for their distinctive embroidery.

q: The Kutch of the Gujarat is famous for:
options: The Kutch is famous for the embroidery, the mirror work, the tie and dye and the Rogan art
It is famous for the wood carving
It is famous for the ivory work
It is famous for the bronze casting
explanation: The Kutch of the Gujarat is famous for the embroidery, the mirror work, the tie and dye, the patchwork and the Rogan art of the natural dyes.

q: The 'Rogan art' of the Kutch:
options: It is the embroidery
It is the mirror work
It is the wood carving
Is the painting with the natural and the vegetable dyes on the cloth
explanation: The Rogan art of the Kutch is the painting with the natural and the vegetable dyes on the cloth and the Chhipi of the Khatri community is the traditional dyer.

q: The Seraikella Chhau was:
options: inscribed in 2010
inscribed in 2005
inscribed in 2021
not inscribed
explanation: The Seraikella Chhau of the Odisha was inscribed on the UNESCO list of the intangible heritage in 2010, along with the Kalbelia and the Ramlila.

q: The Kutiyattam was:
options: not inscribed
inscribed in 2001
inscribed in 2008
inscribed in 2013
explanation: The Kutiyattam, the Sanskrit theatre of Kerala, was inscribed on the UNESCO list of the intangible heritage in 2001, the first Indian element to be inscribed.

q: The 'Yoga' was inscribed on the UNESCO list in:
explanation: The Yoga was inscribed on the Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2006 and it was the first Indian element on the list.

q: The 'Kumbh Mela' was inscribed in:
explanation: The Kumbh Mela was inscribed on the UNESCO Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2017.

q: The 'Buddhist chanting' was inscribed in:
explanation: The chanting of the Buddhist scriptures in the Ladakh region of the Jammu and Kashmir was inscribed on the UNESCO list in 2008.

q: The Kalasha language and the culture of the Dardic peoples were:
options: inscribed in 2008
inscribed in 2003
inscribed in 2013
not inscribed
explanation: The Kalasha language and the culture of the Dardic peoples of the Chamba region were inscribed on the UNESCO list in 2008.

q: The traditional brass and the copper craft of the Utkal is:
options: not inscribed
inscribed in the UNESCO list
inscribed in 2003
inscribed in 2013
explanation: The traditional brass and the copper craft of the Utkal region of the Odisha was inscribed on the UNESCO list of the intangible heritage.

q: The Kumbh Mela, the largest of the human gatherings, is:
options: It was not inscribed
It is the largest of the fairs in India
It is the largest of the human gatherings and it is inscribed on the UNESCO list
It is a religious festival of the Jainas only
explanation: The Kumbh Mela is the largest of the human gatherings on the earth and it is inscribed on the UNESCO list of the intangible heritage.

q: The Mahabodhi Temple of the Bodh Gaya is:
options: the birthplace of the Mahavira
the place of the first council
the place of the Mahaparinirvana
the place of the enlightenment of the Buddha
explanation: The Mahabodhi Temple complex of the Bodh Gaya marks the place where the Buddha attained the enlightenment and it is a World Heritage site since 2002.

q: The Sarnath is the place of the:
options: The Sarnath is the place of the first sermon of the Buddha
It is the birthplace of the Buddha
It is the place of the Mahaparinirvana
It is the place of the Kumbh Mela
explanation: The Sarnath, marked by the Dhammacakkappavattana, is the place of the first sermon of the Buddha and the first Buddhist council.

q: The Ajanta caves have:
options: no paintings
the paintings of the Jataka stories and the Bodhisattva Padmapani
the paintings of the Ramayana
the paintings of the Mahabharata only
explanation: The Ajanta caves preserve the paintings of the Jataka stories and the famous Padmapani panel of the Bodhisattva.

q: The Kushinagar is the place of the:
options: Is the place of the Mahaparinirvana of the Buddha
It is the birthplace of the Buddha
It is the place of the first council
It is the place of the Pancharatra
explanation: The Kushinagar, with the reclining statue of the Buddha in the Mahaparinirvana temple, is the place where the Buddha passed away and it is on the Buddhist pilgrimage circuit.

q: The Lumbini in the Nepal is:
options: It is the place of the Mahaparinirvana
Is the birthplace of the Buddha and it has the Ashokan pillar
It is the place of the enlightenment
It is the place of the first council
explanation: The Lumbini, the birthplace of the Buddha, is marked by the Ashokan pillar erected by the Emperor Ashoka in the third century BCE.

q: The Bodh Gaya in the Bihar is:
options: It is in the Nepal
It is in the Odisha
It is in the Uttarakhand
The Bodh Gaya is in the Bihar and it is on the Buddhist pilgrimage circuit
explanation: The Bodh Gaya, the place of the enlightenment of the Buddha, is in the Bihar and it is one of the four main Buddhist pilgrimage sites in the country.

q: The Taxila in the Punjab was:
options: It was a fort of the Mughals
It is in the Rajasthan
The Taxila was the centre of the learning and the education in the ancient India
It was a Buddhist monastery of the Tamil Nadu
explanation: The Taxila, in the Punjab, was a famous centre of the learning and the education and it was where the Gautama Buddha studied before the renunciation.

q: The Kashi Vishwanath temple is:
options: It is a Buddhist monastery
It is a Jain temple
It is a mosque
The Kashi Vishwanath temple is one of the twelve Jyotirlingas of the Shiva
explanation: The Kashi Vishwanath temple of the Varanasi is one of the twelve Jyotirlingas of the Shiva and it is among the most important of the Shaiva shrines.

q: The Somnath temple is:
options: in the Tamil Nadu
one of the twelve Jyotirlingas and it was rebuilt several times
a Buddhist monastery
a Jain temple
explanation: The Somnath temple of the Gujarat, one of the twelve Jyotirlingas, was rebuilt several times and it is a major pilgrimage site of the Hindus.

q: The Badrinath temple is:
options: one of the twelve Jyotirlingas and it is in the Uttarakhand
in the Tamil Nadu
a Jain temple
a mosque
explanation: The Badrinath temple, one of the twelve Jyotirlingas, is in the Chamoli district of the Uttarakhand and it is among the most visited of the Himalayan shrines.

q: The Rath Yatra of the Puri is:
options: a festival of the Jainas
a festival of the Buddhists
the largest chariot festival of the world and the Jagannath is considered the incarnation of the Vishnu
a festival of the Mughals
explanation: The Jagannath, the Balabhadra and the Subhadra are the chariots of the Rath Yatra of the Puri and the Jagannath is regarded as the incarnation of the Vishnu.

q: The Guru Nanak was the:
options: The Guru Nanak founded the Khalsa
The Guru Nanak was the founder of the Buddhism
The Guru Nanak was the guru of the Mughals
The Guru Nanak established the Sikh religion and the Khalsa was founded by the Guru Gobind Singh in 1699
explanation: The Guru Nanak, the founder of the Sikh religion, was the first of the ten Gurus and the Khalsa was founded by the tenth Guru, the Guru Gobind Singh, in 1699.

q: The Pahari painting developed in the hill states of the:
options: The Pahari painting developed in the hill states of the Punjab, the Haryana and the Himachal
It is a Deccani style
It is the Mughal style
It is the Company style
explanation: The Pahari painting developed in the hill states of the Punjab, the Haryana and the Himachal Pradesh and it is marked by the lyrical quality and the rich colours.

q: The Sita in the Ramayana is:
options: She is the wife of the Nala
Is the daughter of the King Janaka and the wife of the Rama
She is the wife of the Krishna
She is the mother of the Pandavas
explanation: The Sita, the daughter of the King Janaka of Mithila and the wife of the Rama, is the heroine of the Ramayana and of the classical dance forms.

q: The Ramayana of the Valmiki has:
options: 1,000 verses
24,000 verses
about 24,000 verses and the Mahabharata of the Vyasa about 100,000
100,000 verses
explanation: The Ramayana of the Valmiki has about 24,000 verses and the Mahabharata of the Vyasa about 100,000, and the Mahabharata is the longest of the world's epics.

q: The Mahabharata narrates the Kurukshetra war and it is:
options: a devotional work of the Bhakti movement
a philosophical treatise
a collection of the love poems
attributed to the Vyasa
explanation: The Mahabharata, attributed to the Vyasa, narrates the Kurukshetra war between the Pandavas and the Kauravas with the Bhagavad Gita as its philosophical core.

q: The 'Arthashastra' of the Kautilya deals with:
options: The statecraft, the economics, the taxation and the administration
The devotion to the Krishna
The grammar of the Sanskrit
The Buddhist monastic rules
explanation: The Arthashastra of the Kautilya deals with the statecraft, the economics, the taxation, the administration and the warfare, and it is a classic of the political economy.

q: The 'Natya Shastra' of the Bharata Muni is about:
options: The political science
The Buddhist philosophy
The dramaturgy, the theory of the rasas and the aesthetics of the performance
The grammar of the Sanskrit
explanation: The Natya Shastra of the Bharata Muni is the foundational treatise on the Indian dramaturgy, the theory of the rasas and the aesthetics of the performance.

q: The 'Abhinaya Darpana' of the Nandikeshvara:
options: It is a political treatise
Is the earliest of the Indian treatises on the dramaturgy after the Natya Shastra
It is a text of the grammar
It is a devotional poem
explanation: The Abhinaya Darpana of the Nandikeshvara, of the ninth century, is the earliest of the Indian treatises on the dramaturgy after the Natya Shastra.

q: The term Bharata was:
options: a title of the kings
the name of a university
a dynasty
used for the Natya Shastra and later for the Mahabharata
explanation: The term Bharata was used for the Natya Shastra and it later came to be used for the Mahabharata, and the Harivamsha and the Bhagavata Purana were the later additions.

q: The Abhijnanasakuntalam of the Kalidasa is:
options: He was a painter
The Abhijnanasakuntalam of the Kalidasa is the first of the Sanskrit plays to be staged in the modern India
He wrote the Mahabharata
He wrote the Bhagavad Gita
explanation: The Abhijnanasakuntalam of the Kalidasa, which was staged in the modern India by the Kapila Venu and the K. N. Panikkar, is the first of the Sanskrit plays to be revived on the stage.

q: The Nagananda of the Harsha is:
options: a philosophical treatise
a Jain drama
the first romantic play of the Sanskrit literature
a comedy of the Kalidasa
explanation: The Nagananda of the Harsha is the first romantic play of the Sanskrit literature and it was the first of the Sanskrit plays to be translated into English by the R. K. Narayan.

q: The 'Karnabharam' of the Bhasa:
options: Is the thirteenth play of the Bhasa rediscovered in 1912
It is a play of the Kalidasa
It is a play of the Harsha
It is a Jain drama
explanation: The Karnabharam is the thirteenth of the thirteen plays of the Bhasa, rediscovered in 1912 by the T. Ganapati Shastri and staged in 1955 by the K. Balachander.

q: Which of the following statements about the Bhavabhuti is correct?
options: He was a painter
The Uttararamacharita of the Bhavabhuti is a celebrated Sanskrit play
He wrote the Mṛchchhakatika
He wrote the Abhijnanasakuntalam
explanation: The Uttararamacharita of the Bhavabhuti, the celebrated Sanskrit play, is the greatest of the post-Kalidasa dramatists and it centres on the Rama and the Sita.

q: The Ratnavali of the Harsha is:
options: a play of the love of the king and the courtesan
a play of the Kalidasa
a philosophical treatise
a Buddhist text
explanation: The Ratnavali, the third of the three plays of the Harsha, is a romantic comedy about the love of the king and the courtesan.

q: The 'Priyadarshika' of the Harsha:
options: It is a tragedy
It is a historical chronicle
Is a play of the love of the king and the queen and it is a Sanskrit romantic drama
It is a comedy
explanation: The Priyadarshika, the second of the plays of the Harsha, is a romantic drama in the Sanskrit with the love of the king and the queen.

q: The Kavya of the Kautilya is:
options: a play of the Kalidasa
a devotional poem
a grammar
a treatise on the political economy and it is a classic of the Sanskrit prose
explanation: The Kavya, the Arthashastra, is the classic of the Sanskrit prose on the political economy and the statecraft and it is a text of the 4th century BCE.

q: The 'Kamasutra' of the Vatsyayana:
options: Is a treatise on the love and the life and it is a classic of the Sanskrit literature
It is a drama of the Kalidasa
It is a political treatise
It is a Buddhist text
explanation: The Kamasutra of the Vatsyayana, a treatise on the love and the life, is a classic of the Sanskrit literature and it was translated into English by the Sir Richard Burton and the F. F. Arbuthnot in 1883.

q: The Sushruta Samhita is:
options: a philosopher
a painter
a classical text of the surgery and the Sushruta is considered the father of the surgery in the world
a poet
explanation: The Sushruta Samhita, a classical text of the surgery that describes the rhinoplasty, is a landmark and the Sushruta is considered the father of the surgery in the world.

q: The Charaka Samhita is:
options: a surgeon
a poet
a philosopher of the polity
a classical text of the medicine and the Charaka is the father of the Indian medicine
explanation: The Charaka Samhita is the classical text of the medicine and the Charaka is regarded as the father of the Indian medicine and the Ayurveda.

q: The Panini wrote the:
options: He was a painter
The Panini wrote the Ashtadhyayi, the first grammar of the Sanskrit, and the Mahabhashya was by the Patanjali
He wrote the Kamasutra
He wrote the Nagananda
explanation: The Panini wrote the Ashtadhyayi, the first grammar of the Sanskrit, and the Mahabhashya, the commentary on it, was written by the Patanjali.

q: Which of the following statements about the Raghuvamsha is correct?
options: The Raghuvamsha of the Kalidasa narrates the story of the Rama dynasty
It narrates the marriage of the Shiva
It is a play of the love
It is a collection of the sonnets
explanation: The Raghuvamsha, the epic poem of the Kalidasa, narrates the story of the Rama dynasty from the birth of the Rama to the death of the Bharata.

q: The 'Meghaduta' of the Kalidasa:
options: It is an epic of the war
It is a collection of the proverbs
Is a lyric poem of the poet and the separation of the beloved
It is a play
explanation: The Meghaduta, the Cloud Messenger, is a lyric poem of the poet and his beloved and it is one of the masterpieces of the Sanskrit poetry.

q: The 'Gita Govinda' of the Jayadeva:
options: It is a devotional song of the south
Is a poem of the love of Radha and Krishna and it is a landmark of the Vaishnava poetry
It is a play of the Harsha
It is a treatise of the grammar
explanation: The Gita Govinda of the Jayadeva, a poem of the love of the Radha and the Krishna, is a landmark of the Vaishnava poetry and it has been set to the music by many.

q: The Sakuntala of the Kalidasa is:
options: performed in 1900 in Poona
a play of the Harsha
an epic of the war
the most famous of the Sanskrit plays and it was first performed in 1915 at the Writers' Workshop in Calcutta
explanation: The Sakuntala was the first of the Sanskrit plays to be staged in the modern India, in 1915 at the Writers' Workshop in Calcutta, and it was a landmark of the modern Indian theatre.

q: The Dadasaheb Phalke Award of 1969 was:
options: the first to be given and the Ebrahim Alkazi made the Konarak
no award before 1980
explanation: The Dadasaheb Phalke Award was instituted in 1969 and the Konarak, the great theatre of the K. N. Panikkar and the Ebrahim Alkazi, is the finest of the modern Indian theatres.

q: The National School of Drama and the Sangeet Natak Akademi were set up in:
options: set up in 1959
set up in 1947
set up in 1959 and the Sangeet Natak Akademi in 1952
set up in 1975
explanation: The Sangeet Natak Akademi was set up in 1952 and the National School of Drama in 1959, both in New Delhi.

q: The Kalamandalam of the Kerala was:
options: founded by the Rukmini Devi
founded in 1948 in Bombay
a film school
founded by the Vallathol Narayana Menon in 1930
explanation: The Kalamandalam, the Vallathol Narayana Menon founded it in 1930 at the Cheruthuruth, is the premier institution of the classical arts of the Kerala.

q: The Sangam of the Tamil academy is:
options: the association of the poets of the Tamil country
a Buddhist monastery
a temple trust
a modern academy
explanation: The Sangam, the academy of the Tamil poets, was the association that produced the corpus of the classical Tamil poetry of the early centuries CE.

q: The Tiruvalluvar statue of 133 feet was:
options: unveiled at the Kanyakumari in 2000
unveiled in 1980
unveiled in 2010
never unveiled
explanation: The 133 feet tall Tiruvalluvar statue was unveiled at the Kanyakumari on 1 January 2000 and it is a symbol of the Tamil pride.

q: The Dravidian languages of the south are:
options: the Austroasiatic languages
the Tamil, the Telugu, the Kannada and the Malayalam
the Indo-Aryan languages
the Tibeto-Burman languages
explanation: The four major Dravidian languages of the south are the Tamil, the Telugu, the Kannada and the Malayalam, and about a quarter of the Indians speak them.

q: The Nalayira Divya Prabandham of the Alvars is:
options: the philosophical treatise of the Sankaracharya
the epic of the Pandyas
a collection of the love poems
the Vaishnava devotional poetry of the Tamil country
explanation: The Nalayira Divya Prabandham, the hymns of the twelve Alvars, is the devotional poetry of the Tamil Vaishnavas and it is sung in the temple music.

q: The Periyar, with the Self Respect Movement was:
options: a Gandhian
a Marxist of the Bengal
the catalyst of the Dravidian politics in the Tamil Nadu
the leader of the Congress
explanation: The Periyar, with the Self Respect Movement and the Dravidian Federation, was the catalyst of the Dravidian politics in the Tamil Nadu and the anti-caste politics.

q: The 'Bharathidasan' was:
options: He was a Marathi poet
He was a Bengali novelist
He was a Malayalam dramatist
A Tamil poet of the Dravidian movement who wrote the poem of the Paatalai
explanation: The Bharathidasan, a Tamil poet and a leading figure of the Dravidian movement, wrote the Paatalai, an anti-caste epic.

q: The Subramania Bharati was:
options: the Mahakavi of the Tamil and he wrote the Kuyil and the Kannan Pattu
a Sanskrit poet
a Tamil dramatist
a philosopher of the south
explanation: The Subramania Bharati, the Mahakavi of the Tamil, wrote the Kuyil and the Kannan Pattu and he was the contemporary of the Bharathiar.

q: The Ilango Adigal was:
options: He was a Pandya king
The Ilango Adigal wrote the Silappatikaram and was a Jain monk of the Cheras
He was a Chola prince
He wrote the Tirukkural
explanation: The Ilango Adigal, a Chera prince and a Jain monk, wrote the Silappatikaram, one of the Five Great Epics of the Tamil literature.

q: The Appar of the Tamil is:
options: He wrote the Silappatikaram
He was a Jain monk
The Appar was a Saiva saint-poet of the Tamil and a contemporary of the Appar
He was a Chola king
explanation: The Appar, one of the twelve Alvars, was a Saiva saint-poet of the Tamil country and a contemporary of the Appar and the Sambandar of the Seven.

q: The Manikkavacharar was:
options: He wrote the Tirukkural
He was a Pandya prince
The Manikkavacharar, the author of the Sivapprakasam, was the disciple of the Manikkavachakar
He was a Chola king
explanation: The Manikkavacharar, the author of the Sivapprakasam, was the disciple of the Manikkavachakar and a contemporary of the Appar.

q: The Dnyaneshwari, the Marathi commentary on the Bhagavad Gita was:
options: by the Veda Vyasa
a translation of the Ramayana
a commentary on the Upanishads
by the Jnaneshwar
explanation: The Dnyaneshwari, the Marathi commentary on the Bhagavad Gita written in the Dnyana style of the vernacular poetry, is by the Jnaneshwar.

q: The Ramcharitmanas of the Tulsidas is:
options: The Ramcharitmanas of the Tulsidas is the most widely read of the Indian religious epics
He wrote the Mahabharata
He was a court poet of the Mughals
He wrote the Urdu
explanation: The Ramcharitmanas of the Tulsidas, written in the Awadhi, is the most widely read of the Indian religious epics and it is at the centre of the Bhakti movement.

q: The Sur Sagar, a collection of the devotional poems of the Surdas is:
options: a set of the sonnets
the most famous of the Hindi literature
a collection of the love poems
a historical chronicle
explanation: The Sur Sagar, the collection of the devotional poems of the Surdas, is the most famous of the Hindi literature and it is sung in the kirtan.

q: The Mira Bai of the Mewar was:
options: The Mira Bai was a Rajput princess of the Mewar who became the devotee of the Krishna
She was a court poet of the Mughals
She wrote the Ramcharitmanas
She was a Jain nun
explanation: The Mira Bai, a Rajput princess of the Mewar, was the devotee of the Krishna and her poems are the landmarks of the Bhakti poetry.

q: The Kabir of the Varanasi was:
options: He wrote the Ramcharitmanas
He was a disciple of the Guru Nanak
The Kabir was the weaver-poet of the Varanasi and his dohas are the most famous of the Bhakti literature
He was a Sufi of the Sindh
explanation: The Kabir, a weaver-poet of the Varanasi, wrote the dohas that are the most famous of the Bhakti literature and he is venerated by both the Hindus and the Muslims.

q: The Guru Granth Sahib is:
options: It was compiled by the Guru Gobind Singh
It is the eternal Guru of the Sikhs and it contains the hymns of the five Gurus
It contains only the hymns of the Guru Nanak
It is a chronicle of the Mughals
explanation: The Guru Granth Sahib, the eternal Guru of the Sikhs, contains the compositions of the first five Gurus and the later additions of the Guru Arjan and the Guru Gobind Singh.

q: The Basava was a Lingayat saint of the Karnataka and the vachanas are:
options: a Sufi of the Punjab
a Tamil poet
a Jain monk
the famous ones
explanation: The Basava, the Lingayat saint of the Karnataka, composed the vachanas, the short and the direct devotional poems in the Kannada.

q: The 'Akka Mahadevi' was:
options: A Mughal princess
A Kannada saint-poet of the 12th century who wrote the Kannada and the Tamil vachanas
A Tamil poet of the Sangam
A Sanskrit dramatist
explanation: The Akka Mahadevi, the Kannada saint-poet of the twelfth century, wrote the vachanas in the Kannada and the Tamil and she is also called the Mother of the Veerashaiva movement.

q: The Amir Khusrau is best known as:
options: the court poet of the Alauddin Khalji and the father of the Urdu literature
the court poet of Akbar
a Telugu poet
a Persian ambassador
explanation: The Amir Khusrau, the court poet of the Alauddin Khalji and the Bahman Shah, is called the father of the Urdu literature, though the claim is debated.

q: The Faiz Ahmed Faiz was:
options: He was a Punjabi poet
He wrote in the Tamil
He was a scholar of the Vedas
The Faiz Ahmed Faiz wrote the revolutionary Urdu poetry and he received the Lenin Peace Prize
explanation: The Faiz Ahmed Faiz, the revolutionary Urdu poet, received the Lenin Peace Prize in 1963 and the poems like the Mujh Se Pehli Si are the landmarks of the Urdu literature.

q: The Ghalib of the Mughal era was:
options: He was a Persian scholar
He wrote the Ramcharitmanas
The Ghalib was the last of the great Urdu poets of the Mughal era and the Ghazal is his form
He was the court poet of Akbar
explanation: The Ghalib, the last of the great Urdu poets of the Mughal era, is considered the best of the ghazal writers and the icons of the Urdu poetry were the masti and the dast-e-saba.

q: The Premchand wrote the Godan and the Nirmala and he is:
options: a court poet
a philosopher of the polity
called the father of the Hindi novel
a Bengali novelist
explanation: The Premchand, the greatest of the Hindi novelists, wrote the Godan, the Nirmala, the Ghadar and the Raag and he is called the father of the Hindi novel.

q: The Raja Rao of the Kannada is:
options: He was a painter of the Bengal school
The Raja Rao wrote the Kanthapura and he is a pioneer of the Indian English novel
He was a poet of the Bengali
He wrote the Ramcharitmanas
explanation: The Raja Rao, with the Kanthapura, the English novel and the English speech in the Indian idiom, is a pioneer of the Indian English novel.

q: The V.K. Krishna Menon was:
options: the first Education Minister of the British India
the Governor of the Punjab
the founder of the Planning Commission
the first Indian Governor of the Reserve Bank of India and a long serving Finance Minister
explanation: The V.K. Krishna Menon was the first Indian Governor of the Reserve Bank of India and he served as the Finance Minister of the Nehru government for a long time.

q: The R.K. Narayan wrote the:
options: The R.K. Narayan wrote the Guide and the Malgudi Days and the Bachelor of Arts
He was a Punjabi novelist
He wrote the Ramcharitmanas
He was a poet of the Bengal
explanation: The R.K. Narayan, with the Malgudi series and the Guide, is among the most widely read of the Indian English novelists and he was awarded the Sahitya Akademi and the Padma awards.

q: The Mulk Raj Anand was:
options: He was a court poet
He wrote in the Tamil
He was a painter of the Bengal school
The Mulk Raj Anand wrote the Untouchable and the Coolie and he was a founder of the Progressive Writers' Association
explanation: The Mulk Raj Anand, with the Untouchable and the Coolie, was a founder of the Progressive Writers' Association in 1936.

q: The Amitav Ghosh wrote the:
options: The Amitav Ghosh wrote the Sea of Poppies and the Ibis trilogy
He was a Punjabi poet
He wrote the Mahabharata
He was a painter of the Bengal school
explanation: The Amitav Ghosh, with the Sea of Poppies, the first of the Ibis trilogy, and the Glass Palace, is among the most important of the contemporary Indian English writers.

q: The Vikram Seth wrote the:
options: He wrote the Ramcharitmanas
He was a painter
The Vikram Seth wrote the A Suitable Boy and the Golden Gate
He was a poet of the Bengali
explanation: The Vikram Seth, with the A Suitable Boy, the first of the three novels of the set, is one of the best known of the contemporary Indian English novelists.

q: The Salman Rushdie wrote the:
options: He was a painter of the Bengal school
The Salman Rushdie wrote the Midnight's Children and the Satanic Verses
He was a Punjabi poet
He wrote the Ramcharitmanas
explanation: The Salman Rushdie, with the Midnight's Children, won the Booker Prize in 1981 and he was made the Knight of the Order of the British Empire in 2007.

q: The Arundhati Roy wrote the:
options: She was a poet of the Bengali
She wrote the Ramcharitmanas
She was a painter
The Arundhati Roy wrote the God of Small Things and won the Booker Prize
explanation: The Arundhati Roy won the Booker Prize in 1997 for the God of Small Things and she is also a noted activist and a writer of the non-fiction.

q: The Kashmiri literature of the finest sense is:
options: the literature of the Mughals
a Punjabi literature
the oldest of the Sanskrit and it is the tradition of the Kalhana's Rajatarangini
a modern literature
explanation: The Kashmiri literature, one of the oldest of the Sanskrit traditions with the Rajatarangini of the Kalhana, is the source of the medieval romantic poetry of the Vaishnava and the Sufi.

q: The Kalhana wrote the:
options: The Kalhana wrote the Rajatarangini, the chronicle of the kings of Kashmir
He wrote the Ramcharitmanas
He was a court poet of the Mughals
He wrote the Mahabharata
explanation: The Kalhana wrote the Rajatarangini, the chronicle of the kings of Kashmir, which is the finest of the medieval Sanskrit historical works.

q: The Saraswati, the goddess of the learning is:
options: depicted with the lion
depicted with the veena and the swan
depicted with the lotus and the elephant
depicted with the trident
explanation: The Saraswati, the goddess of the learning and the arts, is depicted with the veena, the book and the swan or the white heron, and she is the consort of the Brahma.

q: The Lakshmi of the Hinduism is:
options: She is the consort of the Shiva
She is depicted with the trident
The Lakshmi is the goddess of the wealth and the fortune and she is depicted with the lotus
She is the goddess of the knowledge
explanation: The Lakshmi, the goddess of the wealth and the fortune, is depicted with the lotus and she is the consort of the Vishnu.

q: The Ganesha of the Hinduism is:
options: He is the consort of the Lakshmi
The Ganesha is the god of the wisdom and the remover of the obstacles
He is the god of the war
He is the god of the death
explanation: The Ganesha, the son of the Shiva and the Parvati, is the god of the wisdom and the new beginnings and he is the remover of the obstacles.

q: The Hanuman of the Hinduism is:
options: He is the god of the war
He is the father of the Krishna
He is the god of the death
The Hanuman is the monkey god and the devotee of the Rama
explanation: The Hanuman, the monkey god and the vanara warrior and the devotee of the Rama, is depicted with the strength and the courage and the humility.

q: The Durga of the Hinduism is:
options: The Durga is the goddess of the power and the Shakti and she rides the lion
She is the goddess of the wealth
She is the consort of the Brahma
She rides the bull
explanation: The Durga, the goddess of the power and the Shakti, rides the lion and the ten hands and she is the central deity of the Navaratri.

q: The Kali of the Hinduism is:
options: She is the consort of the Vishnu
She rides the swan
The Kali is the fierce form of the Shakti and she is associated with the Kalighat
She is the goddess of the wealth
explanation: The Kali, the fierce form of the Shakti, is closely associated with the Kalighat temple of the Kolkata and the festival of the Kali Puja.

q: The Shiva of the Hinduism is:
options: He rides the swan
The Shiva is the god of the destruction and the regeneration and he is depicted with the trident and the crescent
He is the god of the preservation
He is the god of the wisdom
explanation: The Shiva, the god of the destruction and the regeneration, is depicted with the trident, the crescent and the third eye and the Ganga flows from his matted locks.

q: The Vishnu of the Hinduism is:
options: He is the god of the destruction
He is the god of the wisdom
He rides the lion
The Vishnu is the god of the preservation and he is depicted with the conch and the discus
explanation: The Vishnu, the preserver of the universe, is depicted with the conch, the discus, the mace and the lotus and he has the avatars of the Matsya, the Kurma and the Varaha.

q: The Brahma of the Hinduism is:
options: The Brahma, the creator, has four faces and four arms and he is the consort of the Saraswati
He is the god of the destruction
He rides the bull
He is depicted with the third eye
explanation: The Brahma, the creator of the universe, is depicted with the four faces and the four arms and he is the consort of the Saraswati.

q: The Navratri festival is:
options: It is a festival of the Muslims
Is the nine nights of the worship of the Durga and it is celebrated across the country with the Garba
It is a festival of the south only
It marks the birth of the Krishna
explanation: The Navratri, the nine nights of the worship of the Durga, is celebrated with the Garba and the Dandiya in the west and with the Dussehra and the Vijayadashami at the end.

q: The Dussehra festival is:
options: It marks the victory of the Kauravas
It is a festival of the Muslims
Marks the victory of the Rama over the Ravana and the effigies of the Ravana are burned
It marks the birth of the Krishna
explanation: The Dussehra, the tenth day of the Navratri, marks the victory of the Rama over the Ravana and the effigies of the Ravana are burned on the Vijayadashami.

q: The Makar Sankranti is:
options: Is the festival of the harvest and the start of the sun's northward journey and the Pongal of the Tamil and the Bihu of the Assam
It marks the death of the Buddha
It marks the birth of the Rama
It is a festival of the Muslims
explanation: The Makar Sankranti, the transition of the sun from the south to the north, is celebrated as the Pongal in the Tamil, the Bihu in the Assam and the Puthineni in the Andhra.

q: The Raksha Bandhan festival is:
options: It is the festival of the harvest
It marks the birth of the Krishna
It is the festival of the Muslims
Is on the full moon of the Shravana and it is the festival of the brother and the sister
explanation: The Raksha Bandhan falls on the full moon of the Shravana and it celebrates the bond between the brothers and the sisters.

q: The 'Milad-un-Nabi' marks the:
options: End of the Ramadan
The beginning of the Islamic year
Birth anniversary of the Prophet Muhammad on the 12th of Rabi al-Awwal
End of the Hajj
explanation: The Milad-un-Nabi, the Mawlid, marks the birth of the Prophet Muhammad and it falls on the 12th of the Rabi al-Awwal.

q: The Hajj is the annual pilgrimage to the:
options: It is a Sikh pilgrimage
The annual pilgrimage to the Mecca and it ends with the Eid al-Adha on the 10th of Dhu al-Hijjah
It is a Hindu pilgrimage
It is a journey to the Vaishno
explanation: The Hajj is the annual Islamic pilgrimage to the Mecca and it culminates in the Eid al-Adha on the tenth day of the Dhu al-Hijjah.

q: The 'Muharram' is the:
options: First month of the Islamic calendar and the Ashura of the 10th commemorates the martyrdom of the Husain
Last month of the Islamic calendar
The month of the fasting
The month of the pilgrimage
explanation: The Muharram is the first month of the Islamic calendar and the Ashura on the tenth of it commemorates the martyrdom of the Imam Husain at the Karbala.

q: The Christmas is celebrated on the:
options: Is celebrated in March
Is a Hindu festival
Is celebrated on the 14th of January
Is celebrated on the 25th of December and it is a public holiday in the India
explanation: The Christmas is celebrated on the 25th of December and it is one of the three national holidays of the Christians in India along with the Good Friday.

q: The Buddha Purnima is celebrated on the:
options: It marks the first council
It is a Jain festival
Is celebrated on the full moon of the Vaisakha and it marks the birth, the enlightenment and the death of the Buddha
It marks the death of the Mahavira
explanation: The Buddha Purnima, on the full moon of the Vaisakha, commemorates the birth, the enlightenment and the death of the Buddha.

q: The Guru Nanak Jayanti is celebrated on the:
options: It marks the founding of the Khalsa
It marks the death of the Guru Nanak
It is celebrated in the Baisakhi
Is celebrated on the full moon of the Kartik and it marks the birth of the first Sikh Guru
explanation: The Guru Nanak Jayanti, the Gurpurab, falls on the full moon of the Kartik and it marks the birth of the Guru Nanak.

q: The Vaisakhi festival is:
options: Is the harvest festival of the Punjab and it marks the founding of the Khalsa in 1699
It marks the birth of the Guru Nanak
It is a festival of the Muslims
It is the Bengali new year
explanation: The Vaisakhi, celebrated on 13 or 14 April, is the harvest festival of the Punjab and it marks the founding of the Khalsa by the Guru Gobind Singh in 1699.

q: The Holi festival of the colours is:
options: It is the harvest festival of the Punjab
Is the festival of the colours that marks the spring and the destruction of the Puthana by the Krishna
It is the festival of the lights
It marks the death of the Buddha
explanation: The Holi marks the arrival of the spring and it celebrates the destruction of the demon Puthana by the child Krishna, and the colours symbolise the spring and the harvest.

q: The Diwali festival of the lights is:
options: Is the festival of the lights that marks the return of the Rama to the Ayodhya
It marks the birth of the Krishna
It is the harvest festival of the Assam
It marks the death of the Buddha
explanation: The Diwali commemorates the return of the Lord Rama to the Ayodhya after the fourteen years of the exile, and the Jai Vilas of the lamps and the Rangoli are a part of it.

q: The Republic Day is:
options: It is celebrated on the 14th of November
Is celebrated on the 26th of January and it marks the adoption of the Constitution in 1950
It is celebrated on the 15th of August
It is celebrated on the 2nd of October
explanation: The Republic Day, celebrated on the 26th of January, marks the adoption of the Constitution of India in 1950.

q: The 'Independence Day' of India:
options: It is celebrated on the 2nd of October
It is celebrated on the 14th of November
Is celebrated on the 15th of August and it marks the freedom from the British rule in 1947
It is celebrated on the 26th of January
explanation: The Independence Day, celebrated on the 15th of August, marks the end of the British rule in 1947 and it is a national holiday.

q: The 'Gandhi Jayanti' is celebrated on:
options: 15th August
26th January
14th November
2nd October, the birth anniversary of the Mahatma Gandhi
explanation: The Gandhi Jayanti, celebrated on the 2nd of October, marks the birth of the Mahatma Gandhi in 1869 and the day is also the National Unity Day.

q: The National Unity Day is:
options: celebrated on the 31st of October, the birth anniversary of the Sardar Patel
celebrated on the 15th of August
celebrated on the 2nd of October
celebrated on the 26th of January
explanation: The National Unity Day is observed on the 31st of October, the birth anniversary of the Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, in memory of the integration of the princely states.

q: The 'Children's Day' in India is celebrated on:
options: 5th of September
15th of August
14th of November, the birth anniversary of the Jawaharlal Nehru
2nd of October
explanation: The Children's Day is celebrated in India on the 14th of November, the birth anniversary of the first Prime Minister, the Jawaharlal Nehru.

q: The 'Teachers' Day' in India is celebrated on:
options: 14th of November
2nd of October
15th of August
5th of September, the birth anniversary of the S. Radhakrishnan
explanation: The Teachers' Day is celebrated in India on the 5th of September, the birth anniversary of the Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan, the second President of India.

q: The 'National Science Day' of India:
options: It is celebrated on the 8th of October
Is celebrated on the 28th of February, the discovery of the Raman effect in 1928
It is celebrated on the 14th of November
It is celebrated on the 5th of September
explanation: The National Science Day is celebrated on the 28th of February to commemorate the discovery of the Raman effect by the C.V. Raman in 1928.

q: The 'Saraswati Puja' is celebrated on:
options: Kartika Purnima
Vasant Panchami, the fifth day of the Magha
Ashadha Purnima
Chaitra Shukla Ekadashi
explanation: The Saraswati Puja falls on the Vasant Panchami, the fifth day of the Magha, and it marks the beginning of the spring and the school season.

q: The 'Kumbh Mela' of the Nashik is also called:
options: The Simhastha
The Maha Kumbh
The Ardh Kumbh
The Kumbhayan
explanation: The Kumbh Mela of the Nashik on the Godavari is the Simhastha and it is held every twelve years, while the Prayagraj one is the Maha Kumbh.

q: The Kumbh Mela at the Prayagraj is:
options: no religious significance
held in the Tamil Nadu
the largest of the human gatherings and the Ganga is central to it
only for the Muslims
explanation: The Kumbh Mela at the Prayagraj, the largest of the human gatherings on the earth, is centred on the Ganga and the Yamuna.
